name: the upgrade page scrolled down to the Max plan
identifier_found: none; the "Get more Claude" title has scrolled off the top; visible text is plan cards ("Max", prices, feature bullets), "Get Max plan", "Limits apply", Terms / Privacy Policy
accessibility_text: only "Close", "Limits apply for Pro", "Limits apply for Max"; nothing names the page
initial_rationale: the page's only title scrolls away with the content and no bar remains; plan names name products, not a place

test_cases.precondition: upgrade page open at the top, "Get more Claude" visible
test_cases.action: scroll down (vertical) past the Pro plan, on to the end of the page (further than the capture), then scroll back up part-way
test_cases.expected_result: the title stays, collapses into a smaller persistent form, or leaves and returns
test_cases.confirms_if: the title is gone at rest and does not return on a partial scroll back
test_cases.overturns_if: the title persists, collapses to a persistent bar, or returns on scrolling back
test_cases.observed_result: "Get more Claude" scrolled out with the content; at the end of the page only the close X, the Max card, "Get Max plan" and Terms / Privacy Policy were visible; a partial scroll back showed "Get Pro plan" and the Pro bullets but no title; no plan was selected

deciding_evidence: live (reached by scrolling the upgrade page, s4): "Get more Claude" scrolls off with the content, no collapsed bar replaces it, and scrolling part-way back does not bring it back — it returns only at the very top. The loss is caused by scrolling, not by navigating. Detector note: the capture reached this state by t20, recorded as a touch on "Everything in Free, plus:"; it is not a structural_same_view_candidate (the header lists differ), so it could not be promoted and no transition verdict is attached — the screen verdict carries the finding.
recommendation: pin "Get more Claude" (or a short "Plans" title) in the top bar beside the close X so it survives scrolling
